name: Savings account
definition: A deposit account generally intended for individuals to hold money while earning interest, subject to product terms.
key_points: Pays interest on eligible daily or average balances
Withdrawals and transaction features depend on the bank and account variant
Fees, minimum balance rules, and limits are product-specific
caveat: Exact rates, fees, limits and eligibility vary by institution, product and jurisdiction.

name: Current account
definition: A transaction-oriented deposit account commonly used by businesses and traders with frequent payment and collection needs.
key_points: Designed for high-frequency transactions with no limit on number of debits/credits
May include overdraft or cash-management facilities subject to credit approval
Typically does not earn interest in most jurisdictions
caveat: Features, charges, interest and permitted customer types vary by bank and jurisdiction.

name: Deposit interest
definition: The compensation a deposit-taking institution pays on eligible deposit balances according to agreed rates and calculation methods.
key_points: Can be fixed or variable depending on the product terms
Calculation frequency (daily balance) and compounding rules (quarterly/monthly) affect yields
Advertised rates may be conditional on tenure or minimum balance
caveat: Do not assume a specific rate or compounding convention without reference to product terms.

name: Fixed-term deposit
definition: A deposit placed for an agreed term, often at a specified interest rate or formula, with structured access conditions.
key_points: Fixed maturity date or tenure ranging from days to years
Premature withdrawal may incur penalty and interest rate reduction
Interest may be paid periodically or compounded to maturity
caveat: Terminology and early break penalties differ across institutions and countries.

name: Home loan
definition: A credit facility provided to finance the purchase, construction, or improvement of residential property, secured by the property.
key_points: Repayment occurs over an agreed tenure through scheduled Equated Monthly Instalments (EMIs)
The underlying residential property serves as primary collateral (mortgage)
Sanction depends on lender policy, borrower income, credit score, and property valuation
caveat: Lending criteria, interest types (fixed/floating), and statutory caps vary by lender and regulatory jurisdiction.

name: Loan eligibility
definition: The formal underwriting assessment determining whether a borrower qualifies for loan sanction and up to what amount.
key_points: Assessed against monthly disposable income, existing liabilities, credit history, and age
Constrained by regulatory caps on LTV and DTI / FOIR
Requires verification of stable employment or business cash flows
caveat: Eligibility rules are institution-specific and never constitute an automatic loan approval guarantee.

name: Credit score
definition: A numerical expression derived from credit report analysis representing the creditworthiness and default likelihood of an individual.
key_points: Calculated by licensed credit bureaus from historical repayment behavior and credit utilization
Higher scores indicate lower historical default risk and qualify for better loan terms
Recent defaults, late payments, high credit utilization, and frequent inquiries reduce the score
caveat: Cutoffs and risk band calibrations differ across lenders and regional bureau models.

name: Debt-to-Income (DTI / FOIR)
definition: A risk metric comparing an applicant's total recurring debt obligations to their gross or net monthly income.
key_points: Used to ensure borrowers retain sufficient uncommitted income for living expenses
Commonly benchmarked in banking between 40% to 55% for retail lending
Known as FOIR (Fixed Obligation to Income Ratio) in Indian banking practice
caveat: Permitted thresholds depend on borrower income tier, employer profile, and lender risk appetite.

name: Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio
definition: The proportion of loan principal relative to the appraised market value of the purchased collateral asset.
key_points: Determines the borrower's minimum required equity down payment (margin money)
Higher LTV implies greater lender credit risk in case of foreclosure
Central banks frequently mandate statutory maximum LTV ceilings to prevent speculative bubbles
caveat: Central bank ceilings and lender appraisal discounts dictate maximum LTV limits.

name: Equated Monthly Instalment (EMI)
definition: The fixed monthly sum paid by a borrower comprising amortized principal and accrued interest over the loan tenure.
key_points: Computed via standard amortization formula: E = P * r * (1 + r)^n / ((1 + r)^n - 1)
In early tenure years, interest constitutes the major proportion of EMI; principal dominates later
Changes in benchmark interest rates may alter tenure or EMI on floating rate loans
caveat: Actual amortisation schedules depend on compounding frequency, rests (daily/monthly), and rate reset dates.

name: Collateral security
definition: An asset pledged by a borrower to secure a loan, which the lender may repossess and liquidate upon default.
key_points: Mitigates credit loss given default (LGD)
Subject to legal title verification, search reports, and independent valuation
May be primary collateral (the asset financed) or secondary collateral
caveat: Enforceability of security is governed by local property and insolvency legislation.

name: Know Your Customer (KYC)
definition: The mandatory compliance framework for identifying and verifying customer identity before entering a business relationship.
key_points: Involves collecting officially valid identity and address documents (OVD)
Includes customer risk categorization (low, medium, high risk)
Mandates periodic customer due diligence (CDD) refresh based on risk category
caveat: Document requirements and digital verification standards are strictly regulated by national financial authorities.

name: Anti-Money Laundering (AML)
definition: The legal and regulatory system designed to detect and prevent financial transactions related to criminal or terrorist activities.
key_points: Requires ongoing transaction monitoring and threshold-based reporting (e.g. Cash Transaction Reports)
Mandates filing of Suspicious Transaction Reports (STR / SAR) to national Financial Intelligence Units
Prohibits tipping off customers under investigation
caveat: Tipping-off rules prohibit disclosing suspicion or reporting to the account holder.

name: Fund transfer & payments
definition: Electronic systems facilitating the movement of money between bank accounts within or across financial institutions.
key_points: Settled either in real-time or in batches via central clearing networks
May involve transaction limits, cutoff times, and processing fees
Includes domestic rails (NEFT, RTGS, IMPS, UPI, FedNow, SEPA) and international messaging (SWIFT)
caveat: Speed, charges, and settlement finality vary according to the selected payment rail.

name: Payment settlement
definition: The unconditional discharging of obligations between two financial institutions upon the completion of a transaction.
key_points: Can occur on a gross basis (RTGS) or net clearing basis
Determines when transferred funds become irrevocable
Regulated by central bank settlement systems
caveat: Rules governing settlement finality depend on the system rules of the clearing entity.

name: Banking customer
definition: An individual, corporate entity, trust, or association maintaining accounts or credit facilities with a financial institution.
key_points: Must undergo KYC and AML screening before onboarding
Classified by legal structure: individual, sole proprietor, partnership, private/public company
Customer data is protected under statutory privacy and bank secrecy obligations
caveat: Confidential customer data cannot be shared across unauthorized systems or external LLMs without masking.

name: Credit risk
definition: The probability of loss resulting from a borrower's failure to repay a loan or meet contractual obligations.
key_points: Managed through underwriting limits, collateral security, risk-based pricing, and provisioning
Classified into stages or grades based on delinquency days past due (DPD)
Loans overdue beyond 90 days are standardly categorized as Non-Performing Assets (NPAs)
caveat: Provisioning norms and asset classification triggers follow domestic banking regulator directives.

name: IRACP Asset Classification & Provisioning
definition: The regulatory framework established by RBI for recognizing interest income and classifying loans into Standard, SMA, Substandard, Doubtful, and Loss categories based on overdue Days Past Due (DPD).
key_points: SMA-0: 1 to 30 days overdue (incipient stress)
SMA-1: 31 to 60 days overdue
SMA-2: 61 to 90 days overdue
NPA: Overdue > 90 days
Substandard asset provisioning: 15% (secured) / 25% (unsecured)
Doubtful 1 (up to 1 yr): 25% secured; Doubtful 2 (1-3 yrs): 40% secured; Doubtful 3 (>3 yrs): 100% provision
Loss assets: 100% provision or immediate write-off
caveat: Classification must be calculated on an account-level DPD basis without subjective deferral.

name: Nayak Committee Turnover Method for MSME Working Capital
definition: A simplified working capital assessment methodology formulated by RBI for MSMEs with fund-based working capital requirements up to ₹5 Crore / ₹10 Crore based on projected annual turnover.
key_points: Total Working Capital Requirement (WCR) is assessed at 25% of projected annual sales/turnover
Borrower must bring in a minimum margin of 5% of turnover as Net Working Capital (NWC)
Maximum Permissible Bank Finance (MPBF) is capped at 20% of projected annual turnover
Eliminates exhaustive balance sheet ratios for micro and small industrial units
caveat: Turnover projections must be validated against GST filings and historical banking churn before applying the 20% formula.

name: Debt Service Coverage Ratio (DSCR)
definition: A fundamental financial health ratio used in corporate and term loan underwriting measuring the borrower capacity to service term debt principal and interest out of operating cash flows.
key_points: Formula: DSCR = (Profit After Tax + Depreciation + Term Loan Interest) / (Term Loan Principal Installment + Interest)
A DSCR >= 1.50x to 2.00x is considered strong and prime for commercial lending
A DSCR < 1.20x breaches standard underwriting risk appetite and requires senior sanction
A DSCR < 1.00x indicates operating cash deficit where company cannot service term obligations from earnings
caveat: Depreciation must be added back only if non-cash; unhedged forex fluctuations must be stressed.

name: Digital Lending Key Fact Statement (KFS) & APR Mandate
definition: Mandatory borrower protection disclosures codified by RBI requiring Regulated Entities to present an itemized one-page summary with an all-inclusive Annual Percentage Rate prior to executing any digital loan contract.
key_points: APR must incorporate interest rate, processing fees, insurance premiums, verification charges, and third-party fees
No undisclosed, hidden, or pass-through charges can be levied on the borrower
Loan disbursals must go directly into the borrower bank account (no LSP intermediary pool accounts)
Mandatory cooling-off period of at least 3 days for loans with tenure >= 7 days (1 day for tenure < 7 days)
caveat: Failure to provide standardized KFS or levy of unapproved LSP fees is a direct regulatory breach under RBI Ombudsman rules.

name: Letter of Credit (LC) & UCP 600 Framework
definition: A binding documentary undertaking issued by an issuing bank on behalf of an applicant (buyer) guaranteeing payment to a beneficiary (seller/exporter) against delivery of conforming shipping and trade documents under ICC UCP 600 rules.
key_points: Governed internationally by ICC Uniform Customs and Practice for Documentary Credits (UCP 600)
Banks deal in documents and not in underlying physical goods (Autonomy Principle)
Strict compliance principle: Documents must match LC conditions precisely without discrepancies
Types include Irrevocable, Confirmed, Transferable, Revolving, and Standby (SBLC)
caveat: Any documentary discrepancy gives the issuing bank the legal right to refuse payment within 5 banking days.

name: Bank Guarantee (Financial & Performance BG)
definition: An irrevocable tripartite legal contract where a guarantor bank pledges to pay a specified financial sum to a beneficiary if the applicant customer defaults on contractual or financial commitments.
key_points: Financial Guarantee: Guarantees payment of a pure monetary liability or debt
Performance Guarantee: Protects project owners against failure to perform construction, supply, or turnkey milestones
Bid Bond Guarantee: Assures tender issuers that selected bidder will execute the contract if awarded
Invoking bank guarantees requires meeting exact documentary terms; courts rarely grant injunctions against unconditional BGs
caveat: Guarantee commitments are non-fund-based credit facilities that convert into fund-based liabilities upon invocation.

name: Customer Due Diligence & Officially Valid Documents (OVD)
definition: The statutory customer identification procedure mandated by RBI KYC Directions 2016 requiring verification of natural and legal persons using authorized identity documents and ongoing risk-based review.
key_points: 6 Officially Valid Documents (OVDs): Passport, Driving Licence, Proof of possession of Aadhaar number, Voter ID Card, NREGA Job Card, and NPR Letter
Quoting of PAN or Form 60 is mandatory for opening bank accounts and high-value cash transactions (> ₹50,000)
Risk-categorized periodic KYC refresh: High risk = every 2 years; Medium risk = every 8 years; Low risk = every 10 years
Centralized CKYC identifier prevents duplicative customer onboarding across Indian financial institutions
caveat: Aadhaar numbers must be redacted/masked (first 8 digits hidden) unless physical offline XML/QR verification is performed.

name: DICGC Deposit Insurance Protection Scheme
definition: Statutory insurance coverage provided by Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation (a wholly owned RBI subsidiary) protecting depositor balances in Indian banks up to ₹5,00,000.
key_points: Insurance limit is ₹5,00,000 per depositor per insured bank (covering both principal and interest across all branches)
Applies across savings, current, fixed, and recurring deposit accounts held in the same right and same capacity
Deposits in different insured banks have independent ₹5,00,000 limits each
Under DICGC Amendment Act 2021, depositors receive payments within 90 days if a bank is placed under RBI moratorium
caveat: Deposits in Primary Agricultural Credit Societies (PACS) or cooperative societies not covered under BR Act do not have DICGC insurance.

name: Priority Sector Lending (PSL) Statutory Targets
definition: Statutory lending quotas mandated by the RBI requiring scheduled commercial banks to direct a specific minimum percentage of credit to underserved economic sectors.
key_points: Overall Target for Domestic Commercial Banks: 40% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) or CEOBE (whichever is higher)
Agriculture Sub-Target: 18% of ANBC (minimum 10% directed towards Small & Marginal Farmers)
Micro-Enterprises Sub-Target: 7.5% of ANBC
Weaker Sections: 12% of ANBC
Shortfalls in PSL achievement are compulsorily allocated to the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) at penalized interest yields
caveat: Banks with PSL surplus can monetize excess credits via market-traded Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs).

name: Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR / Basel III)
definition: The core prudential solvency metric measuring a financial institution capital reserves relative to its risk-weighted credit, market, and operational risk exposures.
key_points: Formula: CRAR = (Tier 1 Capital + Tier 2 Capital) / Total Risk-Weighted Assets * 100
RBI Basel III requirement for Indian Commercial Banks is minimum 9.0% (plus 2.5% Capital Conservation Buffer)
Housing Finance Companies (HFCs) must maintain a minimum CRAR of 15% (Tier-1 minimum 10%) per RBI Directions 2025
Breaching minimum CRAR triggers RBI Prompt Corrective Action (PCA) framework restricting dividend payouts, branch expansion, and lending
caveat: Subordinated debt instruments count towards Tier-2 capital only up to 50% of Tier-1 capital and subject to progressive 5-year amortization.

name: Gold Loan Lending Norms & LTV Cap
definition: Secured credit facility extended against the pledge of gold jewelry or ornaments to individuals for personal or agricultural purposes, governed by strict RBI valuation and margin caps.
key_points: Maximum Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio is capped by RBI at 75% for non-agricultural gold loans
Valuation must be determined using the average closing price of 22-carat gold over preceding 30 days published by IBJA
Bullet repayment option allowed for loans up to ₹2 Lakhs with maximum 12 months tenure
Lenders cannot accept gold coins weighing more than 50 grams or bullion/bars from retail borrowers
caveat: Making charges, stone weights, and precious gems must be excluded from gold weight during official valuation.

name: Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) & Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)
definition: Statutory reserve requirements mandated by RBI to control money supply and ensure banking liquidity.
key_points: CRR is held with RBI in cash as a percentage of Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)
SLR is invested in sovereign G-Secs or gold
No interest is earned on CRR balances
caveat: CRR and SLR default attracts statutory penal interest from RBI.

name: External Commercial Borrowings (ECB)
definition: Commercial cross-border loans raised by eligible resident entities from recognized non-resident lenders under RBI FEMA regulations.
key_points: Available under Automatic Route or Approval Route
Subject to Minimum Average Maturity Period (MAMP) of 3 to 5 years
All-in-cost ceiling benchmarked to SOFR + 500 bps
caveat: Proceeds cannot be used for real estate investment or stock market speculation.
